title: Ch 01 · Paine's two words: the closing sentence
job: The paragraph shows Paine separating society from government.
before: Thomas Paine's pamphlet *Common Sense* reached its readers in 1776, and the edition printed by W. and T. Bradford in Philadelphia is dated February 14, 1776.[^paine_edition]
after: He gave each word its own origin: "Society is produced by our wants, and government by our wickedness."[^paine_wants]

current.text: Paine opened his argument by pulling apart two words his readers used as one: "Society in every state is a blessing, but government even in its best state is but a necessary evil; in its worst state an intolerable one."[^paine_society] The sentence carries the whole pamphlet's frame.
